question: Can supervised adaptation of the last Transformer block improve the already-fitted strong GTE preference model while preserving its lexical and original semantic decision at initialization?
method: LoRA in the query and value projections of the last pretrained GTE attention block only. Rank 8, scale 1, two epochs with 64 pairs per minibatch, AdamW learning rate 0.001 and weight decay 0.04, norm clipping 1, seed 14731. Freeze all original Transformer, classifier, and lexical parameters. Train using pairwise binary cross-entropy on fitting labels. The logit is the original classifier logit plus the change in its signed standardized semantic contribution. A zero update reproduces the parent. A fold-specific parent can be reused only on its own split. The 12288 trainable adapter parameters count as one new supervised fit per learning trajectory.
efficient_input: Cache the pinned model's penultimate token states to float16 using only the training package. Compute the corresponding original final-block pooled output at the same precision and attention mask. All examples stay on the local machine.
comparison: Evaluate the new model and a half-weight blend with its own frozen parent on primary. Only the best positive choice, breaking ties in favor of a single, proceeds to the two separately grouped confirmation folds. Stop at any nonpositive gain. Require strictly positive gain on all three and pooled 0.003 to advance to autonomous course evaluation. At most three additional supervised fits, no model API, no designated validation or test. This distinct study does not change the four registered frozen raw decisions.
